npc.explorer.name: Squid
npc.explorer.1: That torii is older than the village. Under it is the old well - keep going down and you reach the flame.
npc.explorer.2: The ferryman rows out to three islands nobody here has dared visit. Go, and come back and tell me everything!
npc.guard.name: Shrimp
npc.guard.1: Never stand still when they surround you. Roll through the blow, then hit back. The crabs taught me that.
npc.guard.2: Gold you find down there comes home to the village even if you fall. We keep it for you.
npc.trader.name: Tangerine
npc.trader.1: The gold you bring up, I can turn into something that stays with you. You still owe me for those first potions!
npc.trader.2: Sit down. Let's see what the stall has today.
npc.trader.broke: An empty purse, and there's nothing I can do. Go down, and come back heavier.
npc.guide.name: Snail
npc.guide.1: New to the island? There's everything to do here: fishing, cooking, farming, digging.
npc.guide.2: Take on anyone's job and I'll walk you there. Stop, and I'll wait.
npc.guide.lead: Follow me. Stop, and I'll wait for you.
npc.guide.say.lost: Call me when you need me.
npc.guide.say.here.FISH: Rod in hand, sit on the dock (E).
npc.guide.say.here.COOK: In through the cabin door (E), then the cook.
npc.guide.say.here.DIG: Open the mine's gate (E), then the goblin.
npc.guide.say.here.UPGRADE: Talk to Tangerine; see the Upgrades shelf.
npc.guide.say.here.RECEIVE: When the goods come, press E at the carrier.
npc.guide.say.here.KILL: Through the torii is the well.
npc.guide.say.here.REACH: Through the torii is the well.
npc.guide.hint.PET: Open the sheet (Tab), Profile, then the Pets tab to pick a companion.
npc.guide.hint.FEED: Open the sheet (Tab), Profile, Pets, and press Q to feed.
npc.guide.hint.FORGE: Open the sheet (Tab), go to Craft, and forge with stones.
story.intro.1: Awake? The night of the storm I pulled all seven of you out of the shallows. Every one still breathing, too.
story.intro.2: You raved all night about a red tengu that stole your village's flame and tore the sky open to get away.
story.intro.3: It fell straight through this island. The old well has run warm ever since, and things climb out of it every night.
story.intro.4: You keep the village, and it keeps you: food, potions, a forge, a boat. We find your way home together.
npc.worker_farm.name: Goblin farmer
npc.worker_farm.1: The soil here is good. Bring magic seeds and we'll plant them for you.
npc.worker_farm.2: Once it's ripe, someone carries it to your door.
npc.worker_pasture.name: Goblin herder
npc.worker_pasture.1: This pen is mine. Buy the young ones and I'll raise them fat.
npc.worker_pasture.2: When they're ready I catch them one by one and bring the meat to your door.
npc.worker_forest.name: Woodcutter
npc.worker_forest.1: This wood gives timber steadily. Hire us for a spell and you'll have a load.
npc.worker_forest.2: Once it's cut, our lad carries it to your door.
npc.worker_ranch.name: Rancher
npc.worker_ranch.1: Cows give milk, hens give eggs. Hire me for a spell and you get both.
npc.worker_ranch.2: When the pail's full, someone brings it to your door.
npc.worker_fishing.name: Fisher
npc.worker_fishing.1: The water round the island is full of fish. Hire me for a spell and you'll have a basket.
npc.worker_fishing.2: Whatever bites, someone from the road fetches and brings to you.
npc.worker_mine.name: Goblin miner
npc.worker_mine.1: There's orange and sea-blue stone down this pit, and with luck a socket stone. Hire me to dig a while.
npc.worker_mine.2: Once it's dug, someone carries it up to your door.
npc.worker_quarry.name: Goblin quarryman
npc.worker_quarry.1: This quarry gives grey, black and white stone. The longer you hire us, the better the deal.
npc.worker_quarry.2: When it's dug we carry it through the gate to your door.
npc.worker_wool.name: Shepherd
npc.worker_wool.1: These sheep are mine. Hire me for a spell and I'll shear them for you.
npc.worker_wool.2: When it's sheared I'll carry it to your door myself.
npc.worker_kitchen.name: Cook
npc.worker_kitchen.1: Bring good food here and I'll cook it into something to take down the dungeon.
npc.worker_kitchen.2: A full stomach keeps a sword hand steady.

keepsake.santa_letter.name: Santa's letter
keepsake.santa_letter.desc: Left with a present by your bed, one winter's night.
keepsake.santa_letter.text.2: It's me - Santa. I have watched you all year: going down into the deep to keep the village's fire lit, stopping by Cam's stall, feeding the cats, fishing off the pier. This little village is a warmer place for having you in it.
keepsake.santa_letter.text.3: I ask only one thing of you: treasure your sleep. Sleep is the first present every day gives you, before the sun is even up. Don't trade it for one more fight. The monsters below will still be there tomorrow; a good night's sleep, once gone, never comes back.
keepsake.santa_letter.text.4: Your cat gave up its spot so I could leave your present. It grumbled a little, but I think it loves you very much. Scratch behind its ears for me.
keepsake.santa_letter.text.5: A peaceful winter to you, deep sleep and sweet dreams.
keepsake.santa_letter.text.7: P.S. Your chimney is a little tight. It is not the cookies, whatever anyone says.

chess.invite.atomic: A game of atomic chess? On this board every capture goes off.
chess.invite.skeleton: Tonight even the bones in the graves want a game. Sit down for one?
chess.invite.pumpkin: My board is full of pumpkins, and every one hides a trick. Dare you?
chess.invite.ghost: Two of my pieces are ghosts, there one moment and gone the next. Which two?
chess.gist.atomic: A capture blows up its 3x3: both pieces and everything round them but pawns. Blow up their king to win.
chess.gist.skeleton: A piece taken leaves a soul candle and rises three turns on as a skeleton. Skeletons do not capture: they curse the other side's pieces over.
chess.gist.pumpkin: Six pumpkins to begin with, and more every six turns. A piece stopping on one sets it off: a bomb, a scare, a swap, a shield, or trick or treat.
chess.gist.ghost: Each side makes two pieces ghosts: they go through pieces and out of sight, showing when they take, check, or have an enemy beside them.
chess.rules.atomic.1: Chess as usual, with one rule more: every capture goes off.
chess.rules.atomic.2: The blast covers the 3x3 round the capture: the taker, the taken and every piece on the eight squares round them are blown away, pawns excepted.
chess.rules.atomic.3: Blow up the other king and you win at once, even out of check.
chess.rules.atomic.4: A king never captures, and no move may blow up your own king.
chess.rules.atomic.5: Kings standing side by side cannot check each other.
chess.rules.atomic.6: Win by checkmate or by blowing up the king. Ten minutes each; out of time is a loss.
chess.rules.skeleton.1: Chess as usual. Kings are untouched by it all: only checkmate loses.
chess.rules.skeleton.2: A live piece taken leaves a soul candle counting 3, down one at the start of each of its side's turns. At 0, on an empty square, it rises as a skeleton of its old side.
chess.rules.skeleton.3: Skeletons move as before, but a queen, rook or bishop goes three squares at most. A skeleton rook does not castle.
chess.rules.skeleton.4: Skeletons do not capture: they curse. The skeleton stays put; a live piece cursed turns to its side as a skeleton, a skeleton cursed shatters.
chess.rules.skeleton.5: A skeleton that cursed is spent and may not curse on its next turn; a piece just cursed may not curse at once either.
chess.rules.skeleton.6: Six skeletons a side at most; past that, a piece cursed dies for good.
chess.rules.skeleton.7: A live piece taking a skeleton shatters it, leaving no candle.
chess.rules.skeleton.8: After 60 moves each the board is counted: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, skeletons half.
chess.rules.pumpkin.1: Chess as usual. Kings are untouched by it all: only checkmate loses.
chess.rules.pumpkin.2: Six pumpkins begin the game, set out in mirror; every six full turns a pair comes up, six at most.
chess.rules.pumpkin.3: A piece that stops on a pumpkin sets it off; passing over does not. A king treads it flat for nothing.
chess.rules.pumpkin.4: Bomb: the four squares above, below and either side are blown clear, kings excepted.
chess.rules.pumpkin.5: Scare: the other side's pieces round it freeze for their next turn.
chess.rules.pumpkin.6: Swap: your piece changes places with one of theirs, at random.
chess.rules.pumpkin.7: Shield: the first capture of the piece fails, and the shield breaks; a bomb's blast too.
chess.rules.pumpkin.8: Trick or treat: the piece turns into a knight, bishop, rook or queen.
chess.rules.pumpkin.9: An effect that would leave your own king in check fizzles. After 60 moves each the board is counted.
chess.rules.ghost.1: Chess as usual. Kings are untouched by it all: only checkmate loses.
chess.rules.ghost.2: Before the game, choose two of your rooks, knights and bishops as ghosts. The other side does not know which.
chess.rules.ghost.3: Ghost rooks and bishops move and check through one piece at most. A ghost knight may also step one square any way, taking nothing. A ghost rook does not castle.
chess.rules.ghost.4: A ghost that moves without taking goes out of sight. It shows itself when it takes, checks the king, has an enemy piece beside it, or has hidden three turns.
chess.rules.ghost.5: Once shown it stays shown two turns before it may hide again.
chess.rules.ghost.6: Passing over a hidden ghost goes through it; stopping on its square catches it.
chess.rules.ghost.7: A move a hidden ghost forbids is refused: the ghost shows itself and you move again, losing nothing.
chess.rules.ghost.8: Each side has two lanterns (Q): instead of a move, light a 3x3 and every ghost in it shows itself for two turns.
chess.rules.ghost.9: After 60 moves each the board is counted.
chess.resign.title: Resign?
chess.resign.body: This game counts as a loss.
